reference: GNU coreutils unlink invoked by the system Bash when unlink is not an enabled builtin. The one-operand CLI contract and GNU unlink(2) behavior are the independent oracle. Fixture links/directories are created by GNU ln/mkdir in the same private tree.
coverage: Remove an empty or nonempty regular file and compare the resulting tree.
Pass a quoted filename containing whitespace and glob metacharacters literally.
Remove a symlink while preserving its referent.
Remove one name from a multiply linked inode while preserving the other names and contents.
Check directory and missing-path failures without changing the fixture tree.
Exercise GNU CLI operand-count and option-terminator behavior against the loadable's documented name argument.
Check Bash type/help metadata against the loadable's documented help text.
exclusions: No path outside the runner's private relative fixture tree is used.
No system, device, network, privileged, or race-sensitive operation is executed.
Exact diagnostic wording is not asserted for parity failures because GNU coreutils and Bash builtin diagnostics differ by interface.

cases.purpose: A successful unlink removes an empty regular file and emits no output.
A quoted operand containing spaces and glob characters is treated as one literal directory entry; a similarly prefixed neighbor remains.
Unlinking a symbolic-link entry removes the link itself and preserves its regular-file target.
cases.script:
: > target
printf 'target payload\n' > target
command -p ln -s target shortcut
unlink shortcut

cases.purpose: Removing one of three hard-link names leaves the other two names attached to the same inode with their contents intact.
cases.script:
printf 'linked payload\n' > source
command -p ln source first-link
command -p ln source second-link
unlink first-link

cases.purpose: The ordinary unlink operation cannot remove a directory entry of directory type; the directory remains after the expected failure.
cases.script:
command -p mkdir directory
if unlink directory; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A nonexistent relative path reports failure and does not create or remove any fixture entry.
cases.script:
if unlink absent; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU unlink requires one operand; this also records whether the Bash loadable's usage status matches that CLI contract.
cases.script:
if unlink; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU unlink rejects an extra operand before deleting either file; compare that one-operand CLI rule with the loadable's first-argument behavior.
cases.script:
: > first
: > second
if unlink first second; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU unlink accepts -- before an operand; this checks whether the loadable implements the same CLI option terminator or treats it as a pathname.
cases.script:
: > victim
if unlink -- victim; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Help documents the enforced single-file interface and registered builtin.
cases.script: type -t unlink; doc=$(help unlink); [[ $doc == *'unlink name'* && $doc == *'exactly one file name'* ]]; printf 'single-file contract documented\n'

cases.purpose: A future protected-file case can qualify unlink's kernel-level denial path without touching a host path.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed filesystem/syscall mock that can create and verify an immutable regular file (for example, a dedicated disposable filesystem with the required immutable-file capability). The fixture must stay relative and prove the entry and contents remain after unlink is denied. No immutable attribute operation is attempted in this suite.

cases.purpose: An explicit option terminator permits a dash-prefixed file.
An invalid option does not remove the named file.
Help metadata requested with a pathname preserves its bytes; GNU help formatting is not asserted.
cases.script: printf keep > keep; unlink keep --help > usage; [[ -s usage ]]; [[ $(<keep) == keep ]]; doc=$(<usage); [[ $doc == *'Remove a directory entry.'* ]]; printf 'help preserves operand\n'

cases.purpose: Remove a dangling link entry without resolving its absent referent.
